subproblems.title: Locality of approximate tangent spaces (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and A ⊆ B ⊆ U Borel sets with Hⁿ(B ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A and every linear subspace Q of ℝ^P: B has approximate tangent space Q at x if and only if A has approximate tangent space Q at x. Here 'E has approximate tangent space Q at x' is Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 as formalized by HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n E x Q: dim Q = n and ∫_{η_{x,λ}(E)} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as λ ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), where η_{x,λ}(z) = λ⁻¹(z − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U A B : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet B → A ⊆ B → B ⊆ U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (B ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict A), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3, proof of Theorem 1.6 "⇒" (chapter-03.txt lines 113–143), which compares blow-ups of M and of its pieces using the Upper Density Theorem, Ch. 1, 3.6 and Remark 3.7(2) (chapter-01.txt lines 700–725). The Upper Density Theorem is formalized in SimonGMT as Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6 and ae_dimensionalUpperDensity_eq_zero_outside_of_openSigmaFinite (Chapter01/DensityComparison.lean). Notation: Hⁿ = μHE[n]; η_{x,λ}(z) = λ⁻¹(z − x); B_s(x) is the open ball.
1. Put D := B ∖ A, a Borel subset of U. For every compact K ⊆ U, Hⁿ(D ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ(B ∩ K) < ∞. Write U = ⋃_m V_m with V_m := {x ∈ U : |x| < m, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 1/m} (open, with compact closure in U; V_m := {|x| < m} if U = ℝ^P). Then Hⁿ(D ∩ V_m) < ∞.
2. Apply the Upper Density Theorem (Ch. 1, 3.6) to the Borel regular measure Hⁿ and the Hⁿ-measurable set D ∩ V_m of finite measure. For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ D ∩ V_m we get limsup_{s↓0} s^{−n} Hⁿ(D ∩ V_m ∩ B_s(x)) = 0. Let E_m be the exceptional Hⁿ-null set and E := ⋃_m E_m, again Hⁿ-null. Mathlib's μHE[n] is a positive constant multiple of the Hausdorff measure normalization used by SimonGMT, so null sets and vanishing upper densities are the same for both.
3. Let x ∈ A ∖ E. Then x ∉ D (as A ∩ D = ∅) and x ∈ V_m for some m. Since V_m is an open neighbourhood of x, D ∩ V_m ∩ B_s(x) = D ∩ B_s(x) for small s > 0. Hence
 (∗) s^{−n} Hⁿ(D ∩ B_s(x)) → 0 as s ↓ 0.
4. Fix such an x and f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f ⊆ B_R(0), R > 0. Choose λ₀ > 0 with B̄_{λ₀R}(x) ⊆ U, and let 0 < λ < λ₀ and η := η_{x,λ}.
 (a) η is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P, so η(B) is the disjoint union of the Borel sets η(A) and η(D).
 (b) Hⁿ is translation invariant and Hⁿ(λ⁻¹S) = λ^{−n}Hⁿ(S) (Mathlib Measure.hausdorffMeasure_smul₀). So η(B) ∩ B_R(0) = η(B ∩ B_{λR}(x)) has measure λ^{−n}Hⁿ(B ∩ B_{λR}(x)) < ∞.
 (c) Hence f is integrable on η(B), η(A) and η(D), and ∫_{η(B)} f dHⁿ − ∫_{η(A)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{η(D)} f dHⁿ.
5. By (b): |∫_{η(D)} f dHⁿ| ≤ sup|f| · Hⁿ(η(D) ∩ B_R(0)) = sup|f| · λ^{−n} Hⁿ(D ∩ B_{λR}(x)) = sup|f| · Rⁿ · (λR)^{−n} Hⁿ(D ∩ B_{λR}(x)). By (∗) this tends to 0 as λ ↓ 0. For n = 0 the same computation holds with Rⁿ = 1.
6. Therefore ∫_{η_{x,λ}(B)} f dHⁿ − ∫_{η_{x,λ}(A)} f dHⁿ → 0 as λ ↓ 0, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P). Consequently, for every linear subspace Q of ℝ^P, the blow-up integrals of B converge to ∫_Q f dHⁿ for all f if and only if those of A do. The condition dim Q = n is common to both sides. Hence HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q ⟺ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q for every Q.
7. Step 6 holds for every x ∈ A ∖ E, and Hⁿ(E) = 0. So it holds for (Hⁿ⌞A)-a.e. x, which is the assertion. ∎
proof_key_steps: D := B ∖ A has locally finite Hⁿ-measure in U; by the Upper Density Theorem (Ch. 1, 3.6/3.7(2)), s^{−n}Hⁿ(D ∩ B_s(x)) → 0 for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A.
For such x, blow-up integrals over η_{x,λ}(B) and η_{x,λ}(A) differ by ∫_{η_{x,λ}(D)} f, bounded by sup|f| Rⁿ (λR)^{−n} Hⁿ(D ∩ B_{λR}(x)) → 0.
Hence both sets have the same approximate tangent spaces at every such x.

subproblems.title: Integer combinations of integer multiplicity currents, with mass bound (Simon Ch. 6, 3.2(1))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T₁, T₂, S ∈ 𝒟_n(U), p₁, p₂ ∈ ℤ, and let R₁ = (M₁, θ₁, ξ₁), R₂ = (M₂, θ₂, ξ₂) be integer multiplicity triples (IMRep) in U representing T₁ and T₂. If S(ω) = p₁T₁(ω) + p₂T₂(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), then S is represented by an integer multiplicity triple R in U whose measure satisfies μ_R ≤ |p₁|μ_{R₁} + |p₂|μ_{R₂} (as measures). This is Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(1), with a mass bound.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T₁ T₂ S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R₁ R₂ : IMRep U n) (p₁ p₂ : ℤ), IsOpen U → R₁.Represents T₁ → R₂.Represents T₂ → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, S ω = (p₁ : ℝ) * T₁ ω + (p₂ : ℝ) * T₂ ω) → ∃ R : IMRep U n, R.Represents S ∧ R.measure ≤ (p₁.natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) • R₁.measure + (p₂.natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) • R₂.measure
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(1) (chapter-06.txt lines 755–757), which is stated there without proof. The argument uses the orientation conventions of Ch. 6, 3.1 and the locality of approximate tangent spaces (sibling tangent_locality; Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2)).
Notation: R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U, μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M, and R represents T means T(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dHⁿ. An n-vector ζ orients an n-dimensional subspace Q if ζ(α) = ±α(τ₁,…,τₙ) for all n-covectors α, for some orthonormal basis τ of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf). For an increasing multi-index I = (i₁ < ⋯ < iₙ) let dx^I be the n-covector (v₁,…,vₙ) ↦ det[(v_j)_{i_k}]; for n = 0, dx^∅ = 1.
1. Linear algebra.
 (a) If ζ orients Q via the orthonormal τ, then |ζ(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖ (operator norm) for every n-covector α. Also Σ_I ζ(dx^I)² = Σ_I det[(τ_j)_{i_k}]² = det(τ_i·τ_j) = 1 (Cauchy–Binet).
 (b) If ζ and ζ' both orient Q (orthonormal bases τ, τ'), then τ'_j = Σ_i O_{ij}τ_i with O orthogonal, so α(τ') = det(O)α(τ) for every alternating α. Hence ζ' = ±ζ, and Σ_I ζ(dx^I)ζ'(dx^I) = ±1 with the same sign.
2. Setup.
 (a) Since θᵢ ≥ 1 on Mᵢ, Hⁿ(Mᵢ ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{Mᵢ∩K}θᵢ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U. Hence M' := M₁ ∪ M₂ is a Borel subset of U with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞.
 (b) ξᵢ is a.e.-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞Mᵢ. Choose Borel maps ξ̃ᵢ : ℝ^P → Λ_n with ξ̃ᵢ = ξᵢ Hⁿ-a.e. on Mᵢ.
3. Overlap.
 (a) For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ Mᵢ, T_xMᵢ exists and ξᵢ(x) orients it (IMRep).
 (b) Apply tangent_locality to (A, B) = (M₁ ∩ M₂, M₁) and to (M₁ ∩ M₂, M₂). For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ this gives T_xM₁ = T_x(M₁ ∩ M₂) = T_xM₂.
 (c) Let σ : ℝ^P → {−1, 1} be the Borel function σ(x) := 1 if Σ_I ξ̃₁(x)(dx^I) ξ̃₂(x)(dx^I) ≥ 0 and σ(x) := −1 otherwise. By (a), (b) and 1(b), ξ̃₂(x) = σ(x) ξ̃₁(x) for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂.
4. Definition of R.
 (a) Define the Borel function m : ℝ^P → ℤ by m := p₁θ₁ + σp₂θ₂ on M₁ ∩ M₂, m := p₁θ₁ on M₁ ∖ M₂, m := p₂θ₂ on M₂ ∖ M₁, and m := 0 off M'. Let sgn(m) := 1 if m ≥ 0 and −1 if m < 0.
 (b) Let M := {x ∈ M' : m(x) ≠ 0} and θ := |m| (ℕ-valued).
 (c) Let ξ := sgn(m)ξ̃₁ on M₁, ξ := sgn(m)ξ̃₂ on M₂ ∖ M₁, and ξ := 0 elsewhere. Set R := (M, θ, ξ).
5. Pointwise identities. For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M' and every n-covector α:
 (†) p₁θ₁(x)1_{M₁}(x)ξ₁(x)(α) + p₂θ₂(x)1_{M₂}(x)ξ₂(x)(α) = θ(x)ξ(x)(α).
 - On M₁ ∖ M₂ both sides equal p₁θ₁ξ̃₁(α) = |m| sgn(m) ξ̃₁(α).
 - On M₂ ∖ M₁ the same holds with index 2.
 - On M₁ ∩ M₂ (a.e., by 3(c)) the left side is (p₁θ₁ + p₂θ₂σ)ξ̃₁(α) = mξ̃₁(α) = θξ(α).
 Moreover 0 ≤ θ ≤ |p₁|θ₁1_{M₁} + |p₂|θ₂1_{M₂} everywhere, by the triangle inequality.
6. R is an IMRep in U.
 (a) M is Borel and M ⊆ M' ⊆ U. M is countably n-rectifiable, being a subset of a union of two countably n-rectifiable sets (finitely many exceptional null sets and countably many Lipschitz images combine; SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable.mono).
 (b) θ is measurable and θ ≥ 1 on M.
 (c) For compact K ⊆ U, ∫_{M∩K}θ dHⁿ ≤ |p₁|∫_{M₁∩K}θ₁ + |p₂|∫_{M₂∩K}θ₂ < ∞.
 (d) ξ is Borel, hence a.e.-strongly measurable.
 (e) Orientation on M ∩ M₁. Apply tangent_locality to (M ∩ M₁, M₁) and to (M ∩ M₁, M); both are legitimate since Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞. For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ M₁ this gives T_xM = T_x(M ∩ M₁) = T_xM₁. The latter is oriented by ξ₁(x) = ξ̃₁(x), hence by ξ(x) = ±ξ̃₁(x).
 (f) Orientation on M ∩ (M₂ ∖ M₁): the same argument with M₂ in place of M₁.
 So for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, T_xM exists and ξ(x) orients it.
7. R represents S. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ K, K compact ⊆ U. By 1(a), |θᵢξᵢ(ω)| ≤ θᵢ1_K sup‖ω‖ a.e., which is integrable. Using (†),
 S(ω) = p₁T₁(ω) + p₂T₂(ω) = ∫_{M'} [p₁θ₁1_{M₁}ξ₁(ω) + p₂θ₂1_{M₂}ξ₂(ω)] dHⁿ = ∫_{M'} θξ(ω) dHⁿ = ∫_M θξ(ω) dHⁿ.
 The last equality holds because θ = 0 on M' ∖ M.
8. Measure bound. For every Borel set E, step 5 gives μ_R(E) = ∫_{M∩E}θ dHⁿ ≤ |p₁|∫_{M₁∩E}θ₁ dHⁿ + |p₂|∫_{M₂∩E}θ₂ dHⁿ = |p₁|μ_{R₁}(E) + |p₂|μ_{R₂}(E). Hence μ_R ≤ |p₁|μ_{R₁} + |p₂|μ_{R₂} as measures. ∎
proof_key_steps: On M₁ ∩ M₂ the approximate tangent planes coincide a.e. (tangent_locality), so ξ̃₂ = σξ̃₁ with a Borel sign σ.
Define m := p₁θ₁1_{M₁} + σp₂θ₂1_{M₂} (integer valued), carrier M := {m ≠ 0}, θ := |m|, ξ := sgn(m)·(ξ̃₁ or ξ̃₂).
Tangent locality again shows ξ orients T_xM a.e.; the pointwise identity p₁θ₁ξ₁ + p₂θ₂ξ₂ = θξ gives S = τ(M, θ, ξ).
θ ≤ |p₁|θ₁ + |p₂|θ₂ pointwise gives μ_R ≤ |p₁|μ_{R₁} + |p₂|μ_{R₂}.

subproblems.title: Restriction of an integer multiplicity current to a Borel set
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple (IMRep) in U, and A ⊆ ℝ^P a Borel set. Then (M ∩ A, θ, ξ) is an integer multiplicity triple R' in U, and there is S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) represented by R'. That is, S(ω) = ∫_{M∩A} θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ, the restriction τ(M, θ, ξ)⌞A. Moreover μ_{R'} = μ_R⌞A.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U A : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet A → ∃ (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R' : IMRep U n), R'.Represents S ∧ R'.carrier = R.carrier ∩ A ∧ R'.mult = R.mult ∧ R'.orient = R.orient ∧ R'.measure = R.measure.restrict A
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the restriction T⌞A of an integer multiplicity current is used throughout Simon Ch. 6–7 (e.g. Ch. 6, 4.5(2) and 7.2; the proof of 7.2.4 uses R_j⌞W_α and T_j⌞W_i) without a separate printed proof. The argument uses the sibling tangent_locality.
1. Fields of R' := (M ∩ A, θ, ξ).
 (a) The carrier M ∩ A is Borel, contained in M ⊆ U, and countably n-rectifiable as a subset of M (SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable.mono).
 (b) The multiplicity θ is measurable and θ > 0 on M ∩ A ⊆ M.
 (c) Local integrability: ∫_{M∩A∩K}θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩K}θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U.
 (d) ξ is a.e.-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M, hence for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ A) ≤ Hⁿ⌞M.
2. Orientation condition.
 (a) Since θ ≥ 1 on M, Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K}θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U.
 (b) tangent_locality with (A, B) := (M ∩ A, M) gives T_x(M ∩ A) = T_xM for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ A, in the sense that both sides have the same approximate tangent spaces.
 (c) For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, T_xM exists and ξ(x) orients it.
 Hence for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ A)-a.e. x, T_x(M ∩ A) exists and ξ(x) orients it. So R' is an IMRep in U with R'.carrier = M ∩ A, R'.mult = θ and R'.orient = ξ.
3. The current.
 (a) For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) put S(ω) := ∫_{M∩A} θ ξ(ω) dHⁿ.
 (b) Integrability: for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, ξ(x) = ±τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ with τ orthonormal, so |ξ(x)(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖. If spt ω ⊆ K (compact ⊆ U), then |θξ(ω)| ≤ θ1_K sup_K‖ω‖, which is integrable on M ∩ A. So S is a well-defined linear functional.
 (c) Sequential continuity (Simon 6.2.1): if ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U), the supports lie in a fixed compact K ⊆ U and sup_K‖ω_j‖ → 0. Hence |S(ω_j)| ≤ sup_K‖ω_j‖ ∫_{M∩K}θ dHⁿ → 0.
 Thus S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), and R' represents S by definition of IMRep.action.
4. Measure. μ_{R'} = (Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ A)) with density θ = ((Hⁿ⌞M) with density θ)⌞A = μ_R⌞A, since A is Borel and restriction commutes with taking densities. ∎
proof_key_steps: The restricted triple (M ∩ A, θ, ξ) inherits measurability, rectifiability and local integrability.
tangent_locality gives T_x(M ∩ A) = T_xM a.e. on M ∩ A, so ξ still orients the approximate tangent spaces.
ω ↦ ∫_{M∩A}θξ(ω) is linear and sequentially continuous (|ξ(α)| ≤ ‖α‖, local integrability), and μ_{R'} = μ_R⌞A.

subproblems.title: Slicing of integer multiplicity currents by a Lipschitz function (Simon Ch. 6, 4.1–4.5)
subproblems.statement:
Assume (C1), the frozen statement of the sibling-of-parent node dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support: for all P, n ∈ ℕ, open U ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and every integer multiplicity triple R in U representing T, M_W(T) = μ_R(W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, and spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R. Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(U) represented by an integer multiplicity triple RT = (M, θ, ξ), and ∂T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) represented by an integer multiplicity triple RB = (M', θ', ξ'). Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be L-Lipschitz. Then there are currents P_t ∈ 𝒟_n(U), t ∈ ℝ, such that:
(1) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, t ↦ M_W(P_t) is a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ M_W(P_t) dt ≤ L·M_W(T);
(2) for L¹-a.e. t: P_t is integer multiplicity; P_t(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) whose support is disjoint from f⁻¹(t); and P_t(ω) = ∫_{M∩{f<t}} θ⟨dω, ξ⟩ dH^{n+1} − ∫_{M'∩{f<t}} θ'⟨ω, ξ'⟩ dHⁿ for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U).
Remark (no additional claim): the identity in (2) says P_t = ∂(T⌞{f<t}) − (∂T)⌞{f<t} on 𝒟ⁿ(U), which is Simon's formula 4.5(2) for the slice ⟨T, f, t⟩ (Ch. 6, 4.4–4.5).
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = R.measure W) ∧ T.support = U ∩ R.measure.support) → ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U (n + 1)) (RT : IMRep U (n + 1)) (RB : IMRep U n) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (L : NNReal), IsOpen U → RT.Represents T → RB.Represents T.boundary → LipschitzWith L f → ∃ Ps : ℝ → GeometricCurrentOn U n, (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → AEMeasurable (fun t => (Ps t).massOn W) ∧ ∫⁻ t, (Ps t).massOn W ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * T.massOn W) ∧ ∀ᵐ t, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Ps t) ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) (f ⁻¹' {t}) → Ps t ω = 0) ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Ps t ω = (∫ x in RT.carrier ∩ {x | f x < t}, (RT.mult x : ℝ) * RT.orient x (exteriorDerivative (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μHE[n + 1]) - ∫ x in RB.carrier ∩ {x | f x < t}, (RB.mult x : ℝ) * RB.orient x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μHE[n]
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, §4: Lemma 4.1, Remark 4.2, 4.3, Definition 4.4 and Lemma 4.5(1),(2) with their printed proofs (chapter-06.txt lines 1156–1310). These are applied to the (n+1)-current T, so slices are n-currents. The proof also uses Ch. 3, 2.1 (tangential gradient) and 2.7–2.10 (co-area formula, slices of rectifiable sets) (chapter-03.txt lines 327–440), and the hypothesis (C1) for mass identities.
Notation: M, θ, ξ are the fields of RT and M', θ', ξ' those of RB; Hᵐ = μHE[m]. ∇^M f is the tangential gradient of f on M (Ch. 3, 2.1). It is defined H^{n+1}-a.e. on M via the decomposition M = ⋃_j M_j with M_j ⊆ N_j, N_j embedded C¹ (n+1)-submanifolds (Ch. 3, Remark 1.3), and T_xM = T_xN_j a.e. on M_j (Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2); compare sibling tangent_locality). It satisfies ∇^M f(x) ∈ T_xM and |∇^M f| ≤ L. Fix Borel versions. M₊ := {x ∈ M : ∇^M f(x) ≠ 0} and M_t := M₊ ∩ f⁻¹(t).
1. (Lemma 4.1.) For L¹-a.e. t:
 (a) M_t is countably n-rectifiable (Ch. 3, 2.10(2)).
 (b) For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_t, T_xM_t and T_xM exist and T_xM = T_xM_t ⊕ ℝ∇^M f(x) orthogonally (Ch. 3, 1.6 and 2.1, applied on the C¹ pieces N_j).
 (c) Co-area formula (Ch. 3, 2.9 with m = 1, where J^M_f* = |∇^M f|): for every non-negative H^{n+1}-measurable g on M, t ↦ ∫_{M_t} g dHⁿ is L¹-measurable and ∫_ℝ ∫_{M_t} g dHⁿ dt = ∫_M |∇^M f| g dH^{n+1}.
2. (4.3–4.4: the slices.) Fix an exhaustion of U by compact sets K_i. Let Z_bad ⊆ M be the H^{n+1}-null set of points where T_xM does not exist, or ξ(x) does not orient T_xM, or the chosen Borel versions of ξ and ∇^M f differ from the true ones. Let G₁ be the set of t for which 1(a), 1(b) hold, ∫_{M_t∩K_i}θ dHⁿ < ∞ for all i, and Hⁿ(Z_bad ∩ M_t) = 0. G₁ has full measure: use 1(c) with g = θ1_{K_i} (note ∫_{M∩K_i}|∇^M f|θ ≤ L∫_{M∩K_i}θ < ∞), and 1(c) with g = 1_{Z_bad}, which gives ∫ Hⁿ(Z_bad ∩ M_t) dt = ∫_{Z_bad}|∇^M f| dH^{n+1} = 0.
 (a) For t ∈ G₁ and x ∈ M_t ∖ Z_bad (so for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_t) put ν(x) := ∇^M f(x)/|∇^M f(x)| and ξ_t(x) := ξ(x) ⌞ ν(x), i.e. ξ_t(x)(α) := ξ(x)(ν(x)♭ ∧ α) for n-covectors α; there ξ(x) orients T_xM.
 (b) If τ₁,…,τₙ is an orthonormal basis of T_xM_t, then (ν, τ₁,…,τₙ) is an orthonormal basis of T_xM by 1(b). So ξ(x) = ±ν∧τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ and ξ_t(x) = ±τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ orients T_xM_t.
 (c) Hence R_t := (M_t, θ|M_t, ξ_t) is an integer multiplicity triple in U: M_t ⊆ M ⊆ U is Borel and countably n-rectifiable, θ ≥ 1 on M_t, θ is locally integrable on M_t since t ∈ G₁, and ξ_t is measurable.
 (d) Apply the sibling borel_restriction to R_t and A := ℝ^P. It gives P_t ∈ 𝒟_n(U) represented by the triple with carrier M_t ∩ ℝ^P = M_t, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ_t, i.e. by R_t. Thus P_t(ω) = ∫_{M_t} θ ξ_t(ω) dHⁿ for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). For t ∉ G₁ put P_t := 0.
3. Support property. For t ∈ G₁, M_t ⊆ f⁻¹(t). If spt ω ∩ f⁻¹(t) = ∅ then ω = 0 on M_t, so P_t(ω) = 0.
4. (4.5(1): mass.) Let W be open.
 (a) For t ∈ G₁, (C1) applied to P_t and R_t gives M_W(P_t) = μ_{R_t}(W) = ∫_{M_t∩W}θ dHⁿ.
 (b) By 1(c) with g = θ1_W, t ↦ ∫_{M_t∩W}θ dHⁿ is measurable. So t ↦ M_W(P_t) is a.e.-measurable.
 (c) ∫ M_W(P_t) dt = ∫_{M∩W} |∇^M f| θ dH^{n+1} ≤ L ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^{n+1} = L·μ_{RT}(W) = L·M_W(T). The last equality is (C1) for T.
5. (4.5(2): slice identity, following Simon's printed proof.) Fix ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), t ∈ ℝ and ε > 0.
 (a) Cut-off. Let γ : ℝ → [0,1] be 1 on (−∞, t − ε], 0 on [t, ∞) and linear in between. Let h := γ∘f (Lipschitz) and let h_δ be its mollifications: C^∞, h_δ → h locally uniformly, |∇h_δ| ≤ Lip h.
 (b) Since h_δω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and d(h_δω) = dh_δ ∧ ω + h_δ dω,
 (i) ∂T(h_δω) = T(dh_δ ∧ ω) + T(h_δ dω).
 (c) Limits δ → 0 of the outer terms: ∂T(h_δω) = ∫_{M'} θ' h_δ ξ'(ω) → ∫_{M'} θ' h ξ'(ω), and T(h_δ dω) → ∫_M θ h ξ(dω), by dominated convergence.
 (d) Middle term. Since ξ(x) orients T_xM, ξ(x)(dh_δ ∧ ω) depends only on the tangential part ∇^M h_δ = P_{T_xM}∇h_δ. By Simon's step (1), v·∇^M h_δ → v·∇^M h weakly in L²(μ_T) for bounded measurable v; this is checked on the C¹ pieces N_j. By the chain rule (Ch. 3, 2.1), ∇^M h = γ'(f)∇^M f H^{n+1}-a.e. on M, using also ∇^M f = 0 a.e. on each level set {f = c}.
 (e) Letting δ → 0 in (i) gives
 (ii) ∫_{M'} θ' h ξ'(ω) dHⁿ = −ε⁻¹ ∫_{M∩{t−ε<f<t}} θ |∇^M f| ξ(ν♭ ∧ ω) dH^{n+1} + ∫_M θ h ξ(dω) dH^{n+1};
 the integrand of the middle term vanishes on M ∖ M₊.
 (f) Co-area. Apply 1(c) to the positive and negative parts of θ ξ(ν♭∧ω) 1_{t−ε<f<t}, and use ∫_{M_s} θ ξ(ν♭∧ω) dHⁿ = P_s(ω) for s ∈ G₁. The middle term of (ii) equals −ε⁻¹∫_{t−ε}^t P_s(ω) ds, and s ↦ P_s(ω) is in L¹_loc by 1(c) (Remark 4.2).
 (g) Let ε ↓ 0. Then h ↑ 1_{f<t} pointwise, so the left side of (ii) tends to ∫_{M'∩{f<t}} θ'ξ'(ω) and the last term to ∫_{M∩{f<t}} θξ(dω), by dominated convergence. Also ε⁻¹∫_{t−ε}^t P_s(ω) ds → P_t(ω) at every Lebesgue point t of s ↦ P_s(ω). Hence, for a.e. t,
 (iii) P_t(ω) = ∫_{M∩{f<t}} θ ξ(dω) dH^{n+1} − ∫_{M'∩{f<t}} θ' ξ'(ω) dHⁿ.
6. Independence of ω.
 (a) Choose a countable family {ω_i} ⊆ 𝒟ⁿ(U) such that every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) is the limit of a sequence ω_{i_k} with supports in a common compact K ⊆ U and ω_{i_k} → ω, dω_{i_k} → dω uniformly. Such a family exists by separability of C¹_c on each compact piece of an exhaustion.
 (b) Let G₂ ⊆ G₁ be the full-measure set of t for which (iii) holds for all ω_i.
 (c) For t ∈ G₂, each term of (iii) is an integral of ω or dω against a measure that is finite on K (θξ_tHⁿ⌞M_t, θξH^{n+1}⌞M, θ'ξ'Hⁿ⌞M'). So each term is continuous under this convergence, and (iii) holds for every ω. Simon: "by considering a countable dense set of ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) … except for a set F of t having L¹-measure zero, with F independent of ω".
7. Conclusion. The family (P_t) satisfies (1) by step 4. For every t ∈ G₂, a full-measure set: P_t is integer multiplicity (step 2), P_t vanishes on forms whose support misses f⁻¹(t) (step 3), and P_t satisfies (iii) for every ω, which is the stated identity. ∎
proof_key_steps: Lemma 4.1: for a.e. t, M_t = f⁻¹(t) ∩ {∇^M f ≠ 0} is countably n-rectifiable with T_xM = T_xM_t ⊕ ℝ∇^M f; co-area formula on M.
For a.e. t, R_t = (M_t, θ, ξ⌞ν) is an integer multiplicity triple carried by f⁻¹(t); borel_restriction (with A = ℝ^P) gives the current P_t it represents; P_t := 0 otherwise.
(C1) and co-area give ∫ M_W(P_t) dt = ∫_{M∩W}|∇^M f|θ ≤ L·M_W(T).
Simon's mollified cut-off argument gives P_t = ∂(T⌞{f<t}) − (∂T)⌞{f<t} at Lebesgue points; a countable dense family of forms makes the null set independent of ω.

subproblems.title: Local C¹ retraction onto a C² submanifold with ‖Dπ(x)‖ ≤ 1 + c|x − y|
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (U N : Set (Euclid P)) (y : Euclid P), IsOpen U → IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 d N → (closure N \ N) ∩ U = ∅ → y ∈ N ∩ U → ∃ (r c : ℝ) (proj : Euclid P → Euclid P), 0 < r ∧ 0 ≤ c ∧ closedBall y r ⊆ U ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ 1 proj (ball y r) ∧ MapsTo proj (ball y r) N ∧ (∀ x ∈ N ∩ ball y r, proj x = x) ∧ (∀ x ∈ N ∩ ball y r, ∀ v ∈ tangentSpace N x, fderiv ℝ proj x v = v) ∧ ∀ x ∈ ball y r, ‖fderiv ℝ proj x‖ ≤ 1 + c * dist x y
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1(a) of the parent proof (nearest point retraction, tubular neighbourhood theorem: Foote, Proc. AMS 92 (1984) 153–155; Leobacher–Steinicke, Ann. Global Anal. Geom. 60 (2021), arXiv:1811.10578), written out from a chart. The witness π is constructed below as the nearest point retraction onto N near y. Nearestness is a feature of this construction, used only inside the proof; the statement exports exactly the five listed properties. The hypothesis (N̄ ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅ is not needed. B_s := B_s(y); |·| is the Euclidean norm and ‖·‖ the operator norm.
1. Chart. By IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 d N at y there are open V ⊆ ℝ^d, open W ∋ y and ψ with the following properties: ψ is C² on V and injective on V; ψ(V) = W ∩ N; V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W; Dψ(v) is injective for v ∈ V. Let v₀ ∈ V with ψ(v₀) = y. The map ψ|_V : V → W ∩ N is a homeomorphism: it is continuous and injective, and closed because it is proper into W.
2. Tangent projections.
 (a) For v ∈ V let D(v) := Dψ(v) (C¹ in v) and G(v) := D(v)ᵀD(v) (invertible). Then P̂(v) := D(v)G(v)⁻¹D(v)ᵀ is the orthogonal projection onto range D(v), and P̂ is C¹ on V.
 (b) Fix a closed ball V₀ := B̄_{s₀}(v₀) ⊆ V. Put a := sup_{V₀}‖DP̂‖ < ∞ and b := sup_{v∈V₀}‖G(v)⁻¹D(v)ᵀ‖ < ∞. Since G⁻¹Dᵀ is a left inverse of D, |w| ≤ b|D(v)w| for v ∈ V₀ and w ∈ ℝ^d.
3. Normal coordinates.
 (a) Let E := (range D(v₀))^⊥ (dimension P − d) and Φ : V × E → ℝ^P, Φ(v, e) := ψ(v) + (I − P̂(v))e. Φ is C¹, and DΦ(v₀, 0)(w, e) = D(v₀)w + e is an isomorphism ℝ^d × E → ℝ^P.
 (b) By the inverse function theorem (Mathlib ContDiffAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph) there is δ₁ ∈ (0, s₀] with the following properties, where V₁ := B_{δ₁}(v₀) and E_{δ₁} := E ∩ B_{δ₁}(0): Φ is injective on V₁ × E_{δ₁}; O := Φ(V₁ × E_{δ₁}) is open; and Φ⁻¹ : O → V₁ × E_{δ₁} is C¹.
 (c) Shrink δ₁ further so that, for v ∈ V₁, the map (I − P̂(v))|_E : E → (range D(v))^⊥ is a linear isomorphism whose inverse has norm ≤ 2. This is possible because the map is the identity of E at v₀, depends continuously on v, and the dimensions agree.
4. Radii.
 (a) ψ⁻¹ : W ∩ N → V is continuous at y. So there is ρ₁ > 0 with B̄_{ρ₁} ⊆ W ∩ U and N ∩ B̄_{ρ₁} ⊆ ψ(V₁). Moreover N ∩ B̄_{ρ₁} = ψ(V ∩ ψ⁻¹(B̄_{ρ₁})) is compact.
 (b) Let r' := min(ρ₁/2, δ₁/4). Choose r ∈ (0, r'] with B̄_r ⊆ U and 2abr ≤ 1. Put β := ab and c := 2β ≥ 0.
5. Nearest points. Let x ∈ B_{r'}.
 (a) Existence and location. Points of N ∖ B̄_{ρ₁} have distance > ρ₁ − r' ≥ r' > |x − y| ≥ dist(x, N) from x. So dist(x, N) is attained on the compact set N ∩ B̄_{ρ₁}. Every nearest point p satisfies |p − x| ≤ |x − y| and |p − y| ≤ 2|x − y| < ρ₁, so p = ψ(v) with v ∈ V₁.
 (b) Normality. The function w ↦ |x − ψ(w)|² has a local minimum at v, so D(v)ᵀ(x − p) = 0. Thus ν := x − p ⊥ range D(v) and P̂(v)ν = 0.
 (c) Uniqueness. By 3(c), ν = (I − P̂(v))e for a unique e ∈ E with |e| ≤ 2|ν| < 2r' ≤ δ₁/2. So x = Φ(v, e) with (v, e) ∈ V₁ × E_{δ₁}. As Φ is injective there, (v, e) = Φ⁻¹(x) is determined by x: the nearest point is unique, and B_{r'} ⊆ O.
 (d) Definition. Put π(x) := ψ(pr₁Φ⁻¹(x)), the nearest point of x in N. For x ∉ B_{r'} put π(x) := x.
6. Properties.
 (a) π is C¹ on B_{r'} ⊇ B_r, as a composition of C¹ maps, and π(B_{r'}) ⊆ ψ(V₁) ⊆ N.
 (b) If x ∈ N ∩ B_{r'}, then x is its own nearest point, so π(x) = x.
 (c) Let x ∈ N ∩ B_r and v ∈ tangentSpace N x. There is γ, C¹ on (−1,1), with γ((−1,1)) ⊆ N, γ(0) = x and γ'(0) = v. For |s| small, γ(s) ∈ N ∩ B_r, so π(γ(s)) = γ(s). Since π is differentiable at x, the chain rule gives Dπ(x)v = γ'(0) = v.
7. Derivative bound.
 (a) Let g := pr₁∘Φ⁻¹ on B_{r'} (C¹). Then π = ψ∘g on B_{r'}, and by step 5, F(x) := P̂(g(x))(x − ψ(g(x))) = 0 for all x ∈ B_{r'}.
 (b) Fix x ∈ B_r and h ∈ ℝ^P; put v := g(x), p := π(x) and ν := x − p, so |ν| ≤ |x − y|. Differentiating F at x in direction h gives [DP̂(v)(Dg(x)h)]ν + P̂(v)(h − Dπ(x)h) = 0.
 (c) Since Dπ(x)h = D(v)Dg(x)h ∈ range D(v), P̂(v)Dπ(x)h = Dπ(x)h. Hence Dπ(x)h = P̂(v)h + [DP̂(v)(Dg(x)h)]ν.
 (d) Using ‖P̂(v)‖ ≤ 1, ‖DP̂(v)‖ ≤ a and |Dg(x)h| ≤ b|Dπ(x)h|, we get |Dπ(x)h| ≤ |h| + β|ν||Dπ(x)h| ≤ |h| + β|x − y||Dπ(x)h|.
 (e) As β|x − y| < βr ≤ 1/2, ‖Dπ(x)‖ ≤ 1/(1 − β|x − y|) ≤ 1 + 2β|x − y| = 1 + c|x − y|, using 1/(1 − s) ≤ 1 + 2s for 0 ≤ s ≤ 1/2.
8. Conclusion. r > 0, c ≥ 0 and π have all the stated properties; B̄_r ⊆ U by the choice of r. The degenerate cases are included: for d = 0, N ∩ W = {y} and π ≡ y near y; for d = P, E = {0} and π = id near y. ∎
proof_key_steps: C² chart ψ at y; tangent projection P̂ = D(DᵀD)⁻¹Dᵀ is C¹; normal map Φ(v, e) = ψ(v) + (I − P̂(v))e is a local C¹ diffeomorphism (inverse function theorem).
Construction: near y every point has nearest points in a compact chart piece; normality plus injectivity of Φ give uniqueness, and the chosen witness π = ψ∘pr₁∘Φ⁻¹ is C¹ with values in N.
π = id on N; the chain rule along C¹ curves gives Dπ(x)v = v on T_xN.
Differentiating P̂(π(x))(x − π(x)) = 0 gives |Dπ(x)h| ≤ |h| + β|x − y||Dπ(x)h|, hence ‖Dπ(x)‖ ≤ 1 + 2β|x − y|.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Theorem 7.2 and its printed proof (chapter-06.txt lines 2020–2135), "only if" part. It uses the Deformation Theorem 5.3 (lines 1461–1480), the completeness Lemma 3.13 (lines 901–935) and the slicing Lemma 4.5 (here the sibling slicing).
Correction: Simon's localization step ("we can assume without loss of generality that W ⊂⊂ U and spt T_j ⊆ W̄") also needs the localized currents to converge weakly to the localized limit. Step 1 chooses the cutting level so that this holds.
Notation: for integer multiplicity A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and open Ŵ ⊆ U, d_Ŵ(A, B) := inf{M_Ŵ(R) + M_Ŵ(S) : A − B = ∂R + S in U, R ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(U), S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) integer multiplicity} (Simon 7.1). μ_A is the measure of a representation of A, and M_V(A) = μ_A(V) for open V by (C1). For Borel E, A⌞E is the current of sibling borel_restriction. Integer combinations of integer multiplicity currents are integer multiplicity (sibling int_combination). If n > P every n-current is 0 and the claim is trivial (R_j = 0, S_j = 0), so assume n ≤ P.
0. Reduction.
 (a) Fix W open with W̄ a compact subset of U. If W = ∅ then M_W ≡ 0, and R_j := 0, S_j := T − T_j (integer multiplicity by int_combination) work; so assume W ≠ ∅. For each j, d_W(T, T_j) ≤ M_W(T − T_j) < ∞, taking R = 0 and S = T − T_j.
 (b) It suffices to show (★): every subsequence of (T_j) has a further subsequence (T_{j_ℓ}) with d_W(T, T_{j_ℓ}) → 0. Indeed, (★) gives a_j := d_W(T, T_j) → 0. Choosing for each j integer multiplicity R_j, S_j with T − T_j = ∂R_j + S_j and M_W(R_j) + M_W(S_j) ≤ a_j + 2^{−j} then proves the theorem.
 (c) Every subsequence satisfies all hypotheses. So it is enough to find one subsequence of (T_j) along which d_W(T, ·) → 0.
1. Localization (Simon: "by 4.5(1),(2) and an argument as in 6.7(2) of Ch. 2").
 Let f(x) := dist(x, W̄), a 1-Lipschitz function (W̄ is compact and nonempty). Choose δ > 0 with {f ≤ 3δ} ⊆ U, e.g. δ := dist(W̄, ℝ^P ∖ U)/4 (δ := 1 if U = ℝ^P); {f ≤ 3δ} is closed and bounded, hence compact. Put W'' := {f < 3δ} and Λ := sup_j M_{W''}(T_j) < ∞.
 (a) Monotone functions. The functions g_j(s) := μ_{T_j}({f < s}), s ∈ [δ, 3δ], are nondecreasing and bounded by Λ. By Helly's selection theorem a subsequence (not relabelled) has g_j → g pointwise on [δ, 3δ], with g nondecreasing. g is continuous outside a countable set.
 (b) Slices. Write n = (n − 1) + 1 and apply slicing to T_j, with RB the empty triple representing ∂T_j = 0, the function f and L = 1. This gives P_{j,s} ∈ 𝒟_{n−1}(U) with ∫ M_{W''}(P_{j,s}) ds ≤ M_{W''}(T_j) ≤ Λ. For a.e. s, P_{j,s} is integer multiplicity and P_{j,s}(ω) = ∫_{M_j∩{f<s}} θ_j ξ_j(dω) dHⁿ for all ω, where (M_j, θ_j, ξ_j) represents T_j. Fatou's lemma (for a.e.-measurable integrands) gives ∫_δ^{2δ} liminf_j M_{W''}(P_{j,s}) ds ≤ Λ.
 (c) Choice of level. Choose t ∈ (δ, 2δ) such that g is continuous at t, (b) holds at s = t for every j, and liminf_j M_{W''}(P_{j,t}) < ∞; each condition excludes only a null set. Pass to a further subsequence with Λ' := sup_j M_{W''}(P_{j,t}) < ∞. Put W₁ := {f < t}, which is open with W̄ ⊆ W₁, and K₁ := {f ≤ t}, which is compact with W̄₁ ⊆ K₁ ⊆ W''.
 (d) Localized currents. Put T̂_j := T_j⌞W₁ and T̂ := T⌞W₁; they are integer multiplicity by borel_restriction.
 (i) ∂T̂_j(ω) = T̂_j(dω) = ∫_{M_j∩W₁} θ_j ξ_j(dω) = P_{j,t}(ω). So ∂T̂_j = P_{j,t} is integer multiplicity, and M(∂T̂_j) = M_{W''}(P_{j,t}) ≤ Λ' by (C1), because P_{j,t} vanishes off f⁻¹(t) ⊆ W''.
 (ii) M(T̂_j) = μ_{T_j}(W₁) ≤ Λ.
 (iii) T̂_j and T̂ vanish on forms supported in U ∖ K₁.
 (iv) T̂_j ⇀ T̂. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and let s > 0 be small. Take smooth φ_s : ℝ^P → [0,1] with φ_s = 1 on {f ≤ t − s} and spt φ_s ⊆ {f < t}. Then 1_{W₁} − φ_s is supported in {t − s < f < t} ⊆ {f < t} ∖ {f < t − s}, and |ξ(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for unit simple ξ. Hence |T̂_j(ω) − T_j(φ_sω)| ≤ sup‖ω‖ (g_j(t) − g_j(t − s)) and |T̂(ω) − T(φ_sω)| ≤ sup‖ω‖ μ_T({t − s < f < t}). Since T_j(φ_sω) → T(φ_sω),
 limsup_j |T̂_j(ω) − T̂(ω)| ≤ sup‖ω‖ (g(t) − g(t − s) + μ_T({t − s < f < t})).
 The right side tends to 0 as s ↓ 0, by continuity of g at t and because the sets {t − s < f < t} decrease to ∅ and have finite μ_T-measure.
2. Total boundedness (Simon (1)–(3)).
 Let K₂ := {f ≤ 5δ/2} (compact ⊆ U) and M₀ := Λ + Λ'.
 Claim: for every ε > 0 there are finitely many integer multiplicity Π₁, …, Π_N ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with the following property. Let A ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be integer multiplicity, vanishing on forms supported in U ∖ K₁, with ∂A integer multiplicity and M(A) + M(∂A) ≤ M₀. Then A − Π_i = ∂R + S' for some i and some integer multiplicity R, S' vanishing on forms supported in U ∖ K₂, with M(R) + M(S') < ε.
 Proof of the claim:
 (a) Regard A as a current in ℝ^P (extension by zero; spt A ⊆ K₁).
 (b) If n < P, apply the Deformation Theorem 5.3 with grid size λ. It gives A − Π = ∂R + S' with Π = Σ_{F∈F_n(λ)} β_F[[F]], β_F ∈ ℤ. The estimates are M(Π) ≤ cM(A), M(R) ≤ cλM(A) and M(S') ≤ cλM(∂A), with c = c(n, P). The supports satisfy spt Π ∪ spt R ∪ spt S' ⊆ {dist(·, K₁) < 2√P λ}. Π, R and S' are integer multiplicity because A and ∂A are.
 (c) If n = P, embed ℝ^P = ℝ^P × {0} ⊆ ℝ^{P+1} by the linear isometry i. Then i_#A = τ(i(M_A), θ_A∘i⁻¹, (∧_P i)ξ_A) and ∂(i_#A) = i_#∂A are integer multiplicity, with the same masses as A and ∂A. Apply 5.3 to i_#A in ℝ^{P+1} (codimension 1), with support radius 2√(P+1)·λ. Push the result back with the orthogonal projection p : ℝ^{P+1} → ℝ^P; this is defined on the compactly supported currents involved (Ch. 6, 2.23). p is linear with ‖p‖ = 1 and p∘i = id, so p_# does not increase mass and p_#i_#A = A. Since p_#R is a (P+1)-current in ℝ^P, it is 0. Hence A − p_#Π = p_#S'.
  - p_#Π = Σ_F β_F p_#[[F]]. If the P-face F is parallel to ℝ^P × {0}, p maps F isometrically onto a grid cube of ℝ^P and p_#[[F]] = ±[[p(F)]]. Otherwise F contains the e_{P+1} direction, Dp maps its tangent plane onto a (P−1)-dimensional space, ∧_P Dp vanishes on it, and p_#[[F]] = 0. So p_#Π is an integer combination of grid cubes, integer multiplicity by int_combination, with M(p_#Π) ≤ M(Π) ≤ cM(A).
  - S'' := A − p_#Π = p_#S' is integer multiplicity by int_combination, and M(S'') ≤ M(S') ≤ cλM(∂A).
  In the claim, use p_#Π in place of Π, R := 0, and S'' in place of S'. No appeal to Simon 3.9 (Lipschitz push-forward) is needed here.
 (d) Choose λ with 2√(P+1)·λ < δ/2 and 2cλM₀ < ε. Then in both cases the supports lie in K₂ and M(R) + M(S') < ε; restricted to U, the identity A − Π = ∂R + S' (with p_#Π, S'' when n = P) holds in U.
 (e) Finiteness. The cells F ∈ F_n(λ) meeting {dist(·, K₁) < δ/2} (in ℝ^P, or in ℝ^{P+1} when n = P) are finitely many, and |β_F|λⁿ ≤ M(Π) ≤ cM₀. So only finitely many Π, and hence finitely many p_#Π, occur.
3. Cauchy subsequence.
 (a) By 1(d), the currents T̂_j satisfy the hypotheses of step 2.
 (b) Apply step 2 with ε = 2^{−r−1} for r = 1, 2, …. By pigeonhole, choose infinite index sets J₁ ⊇ J₂ ⊇ ⋯ and integer multiplicity Π_r such that, for all j ∈ J_r, T̂_j − Π_r = ∂R + S' with R, S' integer multiplicity, vanishing off K₂ and M(R) + M(S') < 2^{−r−1}. Pick j_r ∈ J_r with j₁ < j₂ < ⋯.
 (c) Since j_r and j_{r+1} both lie in J_r, subtracting the two decompositions gives T̂_{j_{r+1}} − T̂_{j_r} = ∂R_r + S_r. Here R_r, S_r are integer multiplicity (int_combination), vanish off K₂, and satisfy M(R_r) + M(S_r) < 2^{−r}.
4. Summation (Simon (5) and Lemma 3.13).
 (a) Fix ℓ. The partial sums Σ_{r=ℓ}^m R_r and Σ_{r=ℓ}^m S_r are integer multiplicity (int_combination), vanish off K₂, and are Cauchy for the mass M.
 (b) By the completeness Lemma 3.13 they converge in mass to integer multiplicity R^{(ℓ)}, S^{(ℓ)} with M(R^{(ℓ)}) + M(S^{(ℓ)}) ≤ 2^{1−ℓ}.
 (c) Mass convergence implies weak convergence, and ∂ is weakly continuous. So for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), T̂_{j_m}(ω) − T̂_{j_ℓ}(ω) = Σ_{r=ℓ}^{m−1}(∂R_r + S_r)(ω) → (∂R^{(ℓ)} + S^{(ℓ)})(ω) as m → ∞.
 (d) By 1(d)(iv) the left side of (c) also tends to T̂(ω) − T̂_{j_ℓ}(ω). Hence T̂ − T̂_{j_ℓ} = ∂R^{(ℓ)} + S^{(ℓ)}.
5. Back to T and T_j.
 (a) T − T̂ = T⌞(ℝ^P ∖ W₁) and T_{j_ℓ} − T̂_{j_ℓ} = T_{j_ℓ}⌞(ℝ^P ∖ W₁), by additivity of the defining integrals. These are integer multiplicity (borel_restriction) and vanish on forms supported in W₁ ⊇ W.
 (b) Put S̃_ℓ := S^{(ℓ)} + (T − T̂) − (T_{j_ℓ} − T̂_{j_ℓ}), which is integer multiplicity by int_combination. By 4(d), T − T_{j_ℓ} = ∂R^{(ℓ)} + S̃_ℓ.
 (c) By subadditivity of M_W and vanishing on W, M_W(R^{(ℓ)}) + M_W(S̃_ℓ) ≤ M(R^{(ℓ)}) + M(S^{(ℓ)}) ≤ 2^{1−ℓ}.
 So d_W(T, T_{j_ℓ}) → 0 along the subsequence chosen in steps 1–3, which by step 0 proves the theorem. ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce to: every subsequence has a further subsequence with d_W(T, T_j) → 0; then pick near-optimal decompositions.
Localize to W₁ = {dist(·, W̄) < t}: slicing plus Fatou bound M(∂(T_j⌞W₁)); a Helly-continuity level t makes T_j⌞W₁ ⇀ T⌞W₁.
Deformation Theorem: integer multiplicity cycles with bounded mass and boundary mass on a fixed compact are totally bounded in flat distance.
A Cauchy subsequence and completeness (Lemma 3.13) give T⌞W₁ − T_{j_ℓ}⌞W₁ = ∂R^{(ℓ)} + S^{(ℓ)} with masses ≤ 2^{1−ℓ}.
Add back the parts outside W₁, which carry no mass in W, to get T − T_{j_ℓ} = ∂R + S̃ with small M_W.

subproblems.title: Cut-off at a good level: an integer multiplicity cycle X vanishing off B̄_t(y), and the mass of T' + X on B̄_t(y)
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = R.measure W) ∧ T.support = U ∩ R.measure.support) → ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T T' S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : GeometricCurrentOn U (n + 1)) (y : Euclid P) (ρ ρ' : ℝ), IsOpen U → 0 < n → IsIntegerMultiplicity T → IsIntegerMultiplicity T' → IsIntegerMultiplicity S → IsIntegerMultiplicity R → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, T ω - T' ω = R.boundary ω + S ω) → 0 < ρ → ρ < ρ' → closedBall y ρ' ⊆ U → ∃ (t : ℝ) (X Y : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (RY : IMRep U n), ρ < t ∧ t < ρ' ∧ IsIntegerMultiplicity X ∧ BoundaryVanishes X ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) (closedBall y t) → X ω = 0) ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Y ω = T' ω + X ω) ∧ RY.Represents Y ∧ RY.measure (closedBall y t) ≤ T.massOn (ball y ρ') + S.massOn (ball y ρ') + ENNReal.ofReal (2 / (ρ' - ρ)) * R.massOn (ball y ρ')
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the proof of Simon 7.2.4, displays (3)–(7) and (10) (chapter-07.txt lines 187–246), which is steps 5 and 9 of the parent proof. The level is chosen for the single current R, with slicing function f(x) := |x − y| (Simon Ch. 6, 4.5 allows Lipschitz f). So the cutting sets are the balls B_t(y), the level sets are the spheres ∂B_t(y), and F = B̄_t(y). The level depends on the current, so the parent needs no subsequence. Below B_s := B_s(y) and B̄_s := B̄_s(y).
1. Representations.
 (a) Fix representations R̂ = (M̂, θ̂, ξ̂) of R, R_T of T, R_{T'} of T' and R_S of S.
 (b) Apply int_combination to the current T − T' (contract difference) with (p₁, p₂) = (1, −1). Apply it again to ∂R, which satisfies ∂R(ω) = (T − T')(ω) − S(ω), with (p₁, p₂) = (1, −1). This gives a representation RB = (M_B, θ_B, ξ_B) of ∂R.
2. Slicing. Apply slicing to the (n+1)-current R with RT := R̂, RB, f(x) := |x − y| and L = 1. This gives currents P_t ∈ 𝒟_n(U). Note {f < t} = B_t and f⁻¹(t) = ∂B_t.
3. Finiteness. By (C1), I := M_{B_{ρ'}}(R) = μ_{R̂}(B_{ρ'}) ≤ ∫_{M̂∩B̄_{ρ'}} θ̂ dH^{n+1} < ∞, since B̄_{ρ'} is a compact subset of U. Similarly μ_{R_{T'}}(B̄_{ρ'}) < ∞.
4. Choice of t. Let J := (ρ, ρ') and consider three subsets of J.
 (a) E₁ := {t ∈ J : the conclusions (2) of slicing hold at t}. It has full measure in J.
 (b) E₂ := {t ∈ J : μ_{R_{T'}}(∂B_t) = 0}. The spheres ∂B_t, t ∈ J, are disjoint subsets of B̄_{ρ'}, which has finite μ_{R_{T'}}-measure. So J ∖ E₂ is countable.
 (c) E₃ := {t ∈ J : M_{B_{ρ'}}(P_t) ≤ 2I/(ρ' − ρ)}. By slicing (1) with W := B_{ρ'}, the integrand is a.e.-measurable and ∫_J M_{B_{ρ'}}(P_t) dt ≤ I. If I = 0, E₃ has full measure in J. If I > 0, Markov's inequality gives |J ∖ E₃| ≤ ((ρ' − ρ)/(2I))·I = (ρ' − ρ)/2 < |J|.
 Hence E₁ ∩ E₂ ∩ E₃ has positive measure. Fix t in it.
5. Restriction of ∂R. Apply borel_restriction to RB and A := B_t. This gives D ∈ 𝒟_n(U) represented by RB_t := (M_B ∩ B_t, θ_B, ξ_B), with μ_{RB_t} = μ_{RB}⌞B_t and D(ω) = ∫_{M_B∩B_t} θ_B ξ_B(ω) dHⁿ.
6. The cut cycle. Let X ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be the current D + P_t, i.e. X(ω) := D(ω) + P_t(ω). By slicing (2) at t ∈ E₁, for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U),
 (‡) X(ω) = ∫_{M̂∩B_t} θ̂ ξ̂(dω) dH^{n+1}.
 In other words X = ∂(R⌞B_t(y)). This identity only describes the construction; the steps below use it solely in the form (‡), and the statement does not export it.
 (a) ∂X = 0: X(dη) = ∫_{M̂∩B_t} θ̂ ξ̂(ddη) = 0, since d∘d = 0.
 (b) Vanishing: if spt ω ∩ B̄_t = ∅, then dω = 0 on B_t (as spt dω ⊆ spt ω), so X(ω) = 0 by (‡).
 (c) Integer multiplicity: P_t is integer multiplicity (t ∈ E₁) with some representation R_P. int_combination with (p₁, p₂) = (1, 1), applied to RB_t and R_P, gives a representation RX of X with μ_{RX} ≤ μ_{RB}⌞B_t + μ_{R_P}.
7. The current Y. Let Y := T' + X. int_combination with (1, 1), applied to R_{T'} and RX, gives RY representing Y with μ_{RY} ≤ μ_{R_{T'}} + μ_{RX} ≤ μ_{R_{T'}} + μ_{RB}⌞B_t + μ_{R_P}.
8. The open ball B_t.
 (a) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ B_t. Then dω vanishes outside B_t, and R̂ represents R, so (‡) gives X(ω) = ∫_{M̂} θ̂ ξ̂(dω) = R(dω) = ∂R(ω) = T(ω) − T'(ω) − S(ω). Hence Y(ω) = T(ω) − S(ω).
 (b) For admissible ω (spt ω ⊆ B_t, |ω|_E ≤ 1), −ω is also admissible and ofReal(T(ω) − S(ω)) ≤ ofReal(T(ω)) + ofReal(S(−ω)). So M_{B_t}(Y) ≤ M_{B_t}(T) + M_{B_t}(S).
 (c) By (C1) for Y and monotonicity of M_W in W: μ_{RY}(B_t) = M_{B_t}(Y) ≤ M_{B_{ρ'}}(T) + M_{B_{ρ'}}(S).
9. The sphere ∂B_t.
 (a) By step 7, μ_{RY}(∂B_t) ≤ μ_{R_{T'}}(∂B_t) + μ_{RB}(∂B_t ∩ B_t) + μ_{R_P}(∂B_t) = 0 + 0 + μ_{R_P}(∂B_t), using t ∈ E₂.
 (b) By (C1), and since ∂B_t ⊆ B_{ρ'}, μ_{R_P}(∂B_t) ≤ μ_{R_P}(B_{ρ'}) = M_{B_{ρ'}}(P_t) ≤ 2I/(ρ' − ρ), using t ∈ E₃.
10. Conclusion. B̄_t is the disjoint union of B_t and ∂B_t, so μ_{RY}(B̄_t) ≤ M_{B_{ρ'}}(T) + M_{B_{ρ'}}(S) + (2/(ρ' − ρ))·M_{B_{ρ'}}(R). Together with ρ < t < ρ' and steps 6–7, all assertions hold. ∎
proof_key_steps: ∂R = T − T' − S is integer multiplicity (int_combination); slice R by f = |x − y| (slicing).
Choose t ∈ (ρ, ρ') where the slice identity holds, μ_{T'}(∂B_t) = 0 and M(P_t) ≤ 2M_{B_{ρ'}}(R)/(ρ'−ρ) (Markov).
Define X := (∂R)⌞B_t + P_t. The slice identity gives X(ω) = ∫_{M̂∩B_t}θ̂ξ̂(dω) (so X is constructed as ∂(R⌞B_t)); hence X is an integer multiplicity cycle vanishing off B̄_t. Put Y := T' + X.
On B_t, Y = T − S, so μ_Y(B_t) ≤ M(T) + M(S); on ∂B_t, μ_Y ≤ μ_{T'} + μ_{(∂R)⌞B_t} + μ_{P_t} ≤ M(P_t).

subproblems.title: Comparison with the competitor Z + π_#X projected into N
subproblems.statement:
Assume (C1), the frozen statement of the sibling-of-parent node dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support: for all P, n ∈ ℕ, open U ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and every integer multiplicity triple R in U representing T, M_W(T) = μ_R(W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, and spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R. Let P, d, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, N ⊆ ℝ^P an embedded C² d-dimensional submanifold, and y ∈ N. Let r, c, ρ, t ∈ ℝ with c ≥ 0, ρ > 0, 3ρ < r, 4cρ ≤ 1, t < 2ρ and B̄_{3ρ}(y) ⊆ U.
Let π : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be C¹ on B_r(y) with π(B_r(y)) ⊆ N. Assume π(x) = x and Dπ(x)v = v for x ∈ N ∩ B_r(y) and v ∈ T_xN (tangentSpace), and ‖Dπ(x)‖ ≤ 1 + c|x − y| for x ∈ B_r(y).
Let Z ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be minimizing in U ∩ N (7.1.1) with spt Z ⊆ N and ∂Z = 0, represented by an integer multiplicity triple RZ. Let X ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be integer multiplicity with ∂X = 0 and X(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) whose support is disjoint from B̄_t(y). Let Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with Y = Z + X, represented by an integer multiplicity triple RY. Then
μ_{RZ}(B̄_t(y)) ≤ (1 + 3cρ)ⁿ μ_{RY}(B̄_t(y)) + ((1 + 3cρ)ⁿ − 1) μ_{RZ}(B_{3ρ}(y)).

It uses Simon Ch. 6, 2.23–2.24 and 3.3–3.9 for push-forward (chapter-06.txt lines 408–440 and 763–860); Ch. 3, 1.2–1.6 and 2.3–2.6 (C¹ covers of rectifiable sets, approximate tangent spaces, area formula; chapter-03.txt lines 1–143 and 330–410); (C1); and the siblings int_combination and tangent_locality.
Correction of Simon 3.9, used in step 5(c): the multiplicity N of f_#τ(M, θ, ξ) in 3.8 is only a non-negative integer, because oppositely oriented sheets with the same image cancel. For example, an oriented rectangle boundary projected onto a line has zero push-forward, although its image has positive H¹-measure. So Simon's triple (f(M), ζ, N) need not have positive multiplicity on its carrier, as IMRep.mult_pos requires. Step 5(c) chooses Borel versions and restricts the carrier to {N ≥ 1}.
Notation: F := B̄_t(y), G := B_{3ρ}(y), Λ := 1 + 3cρ, μ_Z := μ_{RZ}, μ_Y := μ_{RY}. Write RZ = (M_Z, θ_Z, ξ_Z), RY = (M_Y, θ_Y, ξ_Y), and fix a representation RX = (M_X, θ_X, ξ_X) of X. Dπ(x) is the Fréchet derivative (fderiv) of π at x, and ‖·‖ is the operator norm.
Multilinear algebra:
- For an n-covector α and a linear map L, α∘L is the covector (v₁, …, vₙ) ↦ α(Lv₁, …, Lvₙ).
- An n-vector is a linear functional ζ on n-covectors (MultiVector), and (∧ₙL)ζ is the n-vector α ↦ ζ(α∘L).
- For increasing I = (i₁ < ⋯ < iₙ), dx^I is the coordinate covector (v₁, …, vₙ) ↦ det[(v_j)_{i_k}], and e_I := (e_{i₁}, …, e_{iₙ}). Then α = Σ_I α(e_I)dx^I, and the coordinates ζ(dx^I) determine ζ.
- |α|_E := (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean coefficient norm used in M_W, and |ζ| := (Σ_I ζ(dx^I)²)^{1/2}.
- A unit orientation of an n-dimensional subspace Π is an n-vector ζ with ζ(α) = ±α(σ₁, …, σₙ) for all α, for an orthonormal basis σ of Π (IsUnitOrientationOf).
Four facts are used below.
 (L1) |α(v₁, …, vₙ)| ≤ |α|_E·Π_j|v_j|. This follows from α(v) = Σ_I α(e_I)det[(v_j)_I], Cauchy–Schwarz, Cauchy–Binet (Σ_I det[(v_j)_I]² = det(v_i·v_j)) and Hadamard (det(v_i·v_j) ≤ Π_j|v_j|²). Also |α(v)| ≤ ‖α‖·Π_j|v_j| for the operator norm ‖α‖.
 (L2) A unit orientation ζ of Π has |ζ| = 1, by Cauchy–Binet. For every n-vector ζ, |ζ(α)| ≤ |ζ||α|_E, by Cauchy–Schwarz in the coordinates.
 (L3) Two unit orientations of the same Π differ by a sign: orthonormal bases of Π differ by an orthogonal matrix O, and α(σO) = det(O)α(σ) with det(O) = ±1.
 (L4) Let ζ(α) = ±α(τ₁, …, τₙ) for an orthonormal basis τ of an n-plane P₀, and let L be linear. Then (∧ₙL)ζ(α) = ±α(Lτ₁, …, Lτₙ) and |(∧ₙL)ζ| = det(Lτ_i·Lτ_j)^{1/2} ≤ ‖L‖ⁿ. If |(∧ₙL)ζ| = 0, then (∧ₙL)ζ = 0. If |(∧ₙL)ζ| > 0, then L is injective on P₀ and L(P₀) is an n-plane. Writing Lτ_j = Σ_l B_{lj}σ_l for an orthonormal basis σ of L(P₀) gives (∧ₙL)ζ(α) = ±det(B)α(σ) with |det B| = |(∧ₙL)ζ|. So (∧ₙL)ζ/|(∧ₙL)ζ| is a unit orientation of L(P₀).
If t < 0 then F = ∅ and the claim is trivial, so assume t ≥ 0. Then F ⊆ B_{2ρ}(y) ⊆ G, and Ḡ = B̄_{3ρ}(y) ⊆ B_r(y) ∩ U is compact.
1. Lipschitz bounds and π(F).
 (a) For 0 < s < r the closed ball B̄_s(y) ⊆ B_r(y) is convex, π is differentiable on it, and ‖Dπ‖ ≤ 1 + cs there. By the mean value inequality (Mathlib Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le), |π(x) − π(x')| ≤ (1 + cs)|x − x'| for x, x' ∈ B̄_s(y). In particular π is Λ-Lipschitz on B̄_{2ρ}(y), since 2ρ < r and 1 + 2cρ ≤ Λ. Hence Hⁿ(π(A)) ≤ ΛⁿHⁿ(A) for every A ⊆ B̄_{2ρ}(y).
 (b) π(y) = y, since y ∈ N ∩ B_r(y).
 (c) For x ∈ F: |π(x) − y| ≤ (1 + ct)t ≤ (1 + 2cρ)t < (3/2)(2ρ) = 3ρ, using 4cρ ≤ 1. Also π(x) ∈ N, since F ⊆ B_r(y). So K' := π(F) is a compact subset of N ∩ G ⊆ U.
 (d) Let p₀ be the nearest point projection of ℝ^P onto the closed convex ball B̄_{2ρ}(y); it is 1-Lipschitz. Then π̃ := π∘p₀ is Λ-Lipschitz on ℝ^P and agrees with π on B̄_{2ρ}(y) ⊇ F.
2. Consequences of (C1).
 (a) μ_X(ℝ^P ∖ F) = 0. U ∖ F is open, and X vanishes on every form admissible for M_{U∖F}(X), since such a form has support disjoint from F. So μ_X(U ∖ F) = M_{U∖F}(X) = 0, and μ_X(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0. Since θ_X ≥ 1, Hⁿ(M_X ∖ F) = 0.
 (b) μ_Z(U ∖ N) = 0. By (C1), U ∩ spt μ_Z = spt Z ⊆ N. So U ∖ N ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ spt μ_Z, which is μ_Z-null (Mathlib measure_compl_support). Hence Hⁿ(M_Z ∖ N) = 0.
 (c) For every open V ⊆ U ∖ F we have Y(ω) = Z(ω) + X(ω) = Z(ω) when spt ω ⊆ V. Hence μ_Y(V) = M_V(Y) = M_V(Z) = μ_Z(V).
 (d) μ_Z(G) = M_G(Z) < ∞, μ_Y(G) < ∞ and ∫_{M_X∩F} θ_X dHⁿ < ∞. These follow from local integrability on the compact sets Ḡ ⊆ U and F ⊆ U.
3. Tangent inclusion. Claim: for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_Z, x ∈ N, T_xM_Z =: Q exists, ξ_Z(x) orients Q, and Q ⊆ tangentSpace N x. The first three hold a.e. by 2(b) and the IMRep property. Fix such an x, a chart ψ : V → W of N at x with x = ψ(v_x), and put L := range Dψ(v_x).
 (a) L ⊆ tangentSpace N x. Let w ∈ ℝ^d and choose δ > 0 with B̄_δ(v_x) ⊆ V. Let κ(s) := (δ/(1 + |w|)) tanh(s(1 + |w|)/δ). Then γ(s) := ψ(v_x + κ(s)w) is C¹ on ℝ, γ(ℝ) ⊆ ψ(V) ⊆ N, γ(0) = x and γ'(0) = Dψ(v_x)w.
 (b) Flatness of N at x. ψ|_V is a homeomorphism onto N ∩ W and Dψ(v_x) is injective. So for z ∈ N near x, z = ψ(v) with v near v_x, |v − v_x| ≤ C|z − x|, and dist(z − x, L) = o(|z − x|) as z → x.
 (c) Q ⊆ L. Suppose p ∈ Q ∖ L. Choose δ' > 0 with B_{3δ'}(p) ∩ L = ∅. By (b), for small λ > 0 every z ∈ N with (z − x)/λ ∈ B_{δ'}(p) has dist((z − x)/λ, L) < δ', which is impossible. So η_{x,λ}(N) ∩ B_{δ'}(p) = ∅, and η_{x,λ}(M_Z) ∩ B_{δ'}(p) ⊆ η_{x,λ}(M_Z ∖ N), an Hⁿ-null set.
 (d) Contradiction. Take f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with 0 ≤ f ≤ 1, f = 1 on B_{δ'/2}(p) and spt f ⊆ B_{δ'}(p). Then ∫_{η_{x,λ}(M_Z)} f dHⁿ = 0 for small λ, whereas its limit must be ∫_Q f dHⁿ ≥ Hⁿ(Q ∩ B_{δ'/2}(p)) > 0. Hence Q ⊆ L ⊆ tangentSpace N x.
4. π fixes Z. For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_Z ∩ G we have x ∈ N ∩ B_r(y) and π(x) = x. Write ξ_Z(x)(α) = ±α(τ) with τ an orthonormal basis of Q ⊆ tangentSpace N x. Then Dπ(x)τᵢ = τᵢ, so ξ_Z(x)(α∘Dπ(x)) = ξ_Z(x)(α) for every n-covector α. In particular ξ_Z(x)(ω(x)) = ξ_Z(x)(ω(π(x))∘Dπ(x)) for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U).
5. The projected cycle Q_π := π_#X. Define Q_π(ω) := ∫_{M_X∩F} θ_X ξ_X(ω(π(x))∘Dπ(x)) dHⁿ(x) for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). This is Simon 2.24(2), 3.3–3.6 for the C¹ map π, which is proper on the compact F; μ_X is carried by F by 2(a).
 (a) Current. The integrand is Hⁿ⌞(M_X ∩ F)-a.e. strongly measurable, since x ↦ ω(π(x))∘Dπ(x) is continuous on B_r(y) ⊇ F. For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_X, ξ_X(x) is a unit orientation. So by (L1) and ‖Dπ‖ ≤ Λ on F, |ξ_X(x)(α∘Dπ(x))| ≤ ‖α‖Λⁿ. Hence |Q_π(ω)| ≤ Λⁿ·sup_x‖ω(x)‖·∫_{M_X∩F} θ_X dHⁿ, which is finite by 2(d). Q_π is linear. If ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U), then sup‖ω_j‖ → 0, so Q_π(ω_j) → 0. Thus Q_π is a GeometricCurrentOn U n.
 (b) Support. If ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) vanishes on K' = π(F), then Q_π(ω) = 0. Every z ∈ U ∖ K' has a ball B_s(z) whose closure is a compact subset of the open set U ∖ K'. Q_π vanishes on forms supported in B_s(z), so z lies in the zero region of Q_π. Hence spt Q_π ⊆ K'. As spt Q_π is relatively closed in U and contained in the compact K' ⊆ U, it is compact. It is contained in K' ⊆ (U ∩ N) ∩ G.
 (c) Integer multiplicity. We construct an IMRep R_Q = (C, N', ζ') in U representing Q_π. This is Simon 3.3–3.9 with the correction stated at the top.
  (c1) Set-up. Put M := M_X ∩ F and θ := θ_X. M is Borel and countably n-rectifiable, being a subset of M_X (SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable.mono). By 2(d), Hⁿ(M) ≤ ∫_M θ dHⁿ < ∞. Fix a Borel map ξ̃ : ℝ^P → Λ_n with ξ̃ = ξ_X Hⁿ-a.e. on M. Call x ∈ M oriented if T_xM exists and ξ̃(x) is a unit orientation of it. Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M is oriented: a.e. on M, T_xM_X exists and is oriented by ξ_X(x) = ξ̃(x) (IMRep), and tangent_locality with (A, B) = (M, M_X) gives T_xM = T_xM_X. Define the Borel function J(x) := |(∧ₙDπ(x))ξ̃(x)| on M. By (L4), at an oriented x, J(x) is the Jacobian J^M_π(x) of Simon Ch. 3, 2.3, and J(x) ≤ ‖Dπ(x)‖ⁿ ≤ Λⁿ. Let M₊ := {x ∈ M : J(x) > 0}, a Borel set. For x ∈ M ∖ M₊ the n-vector (∧ₙDπ(x))ξ̃(x) is 0, since its norm is 0.
  (c2) C¹ pieces on which π is injective. By Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 and Remark 1.3, M = ⋃_{j≥0} M_j disjointly, with M_j Borel, Hⁿ(M₀) = 0, and M_j ⊆ N_j for embedded C¹ n-submanifolds N_j (j ≥ 1). SimonGMT simon_remark_1_3 gives the disjoint Borel pieces: the N_j are Borel (SimonGMT measurableSet_of_isSimonSubmanifold), and a Borel null N₀ ⊇ M₀ exists because Hⁿ is Borel regular. By Remark 1.5(2), T_xM = T_xN_j for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_j.
   Let x₀ ∈ N_j ∩ B_{2ρ}(y) with Dπ(x₀) injective on T_{x₀}N_j. Take a C¹ parametrization φ of N_j near x₀, with φ(v₀) = x₀ and Dφ(v₀) an isomorphism onto T_{x₀}N_j. Then π∘φ is C¹ with injective derivative at v₀. By the inverse function theorem, in the form of the local immersion theorem (Simon Ch. 6, 3.4), there is an open set O ∋ x₀ with O ⊆ B_{2ρ}(y) such that:
   - π is injective on N_j ∩ O;
   - Σ := π(N_j ∩ O) is an embedded C¹ n-submanifold with Hⁿ(Σ) < ∞ (take N_j ∩ O = φ(V'') with V'' bounded, of compact closure in the domain of φ);
   - T_{π(z)}Σ = Dπ(z)(T_zN_j) for z ∈ N_j ∩ O.
   By Lindelöf's theorem, for each j countably many such O cover {x ∈ N_j ∩ B_{2ρ}(y) : Dπ(x) is injective on T_xN_j}. Enumerate all of them, over all j, as (j(k), O_k, Σ_k), k = 1, 2, …. Put A_k := (M₊ ∩ M_{j(k)} ∩ O_k) ∖ ⋃_{k'<k} A_{k'}; these are Borel and pairwise disjoint.
   Let x ∈ M₊ ∩ M_j (j ≥ 1) be oriented with T_xM = T_xN_j. Then Dπ(x) is injective on T_xN_j, by (L4) as J(x) > 0, and x ∈ F ⊆ B_{2ρ}(y); so x ∈ ⋃_k A_k. Hence Hⁿ(M₊ ∖ ⋃_k A_k) = 0. Moreover, π is injective on each A_k, π(A_k) ⊆ Σ_k, and Dπ(x)(T_xM) = T_{π(x)}Σ_k for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A_k.
  (c3) Compact pieces and the image set. Hⁿ⌞M is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P, hence inner regular. For each k choose compact sets K_{k,1}, K_{k,2}, … with K_{k,i} ⊆ A_k ∖ (K_{k,1} ∪ ⋯ ∪ K_{k,i−1}) and Hⁿ(A_k ∖ (K_{k,1} ∪ ⋯ ∪ K_{k,i})) < 2^{−i}. Enumerate all K_{k,i} as K₁, K₂, …; they are pairwise disjoint, with K_m ⊆ A_{k(m)}.
   Put M' := ⋃_m K_m ⊆ M₊, a Borel set with Hⁿ(M₊ ∖ M') = 0, and E := π(M') = ⋃_m π(K_m). Each π(K_m) is compact, so E is σ-compact, hence Borel. Also E ⊆ K' ⊆ G ⊆ U, E ⊆ ⋃_k Σ_k, and Hⁿ(E) ≤ ΛⁿHⁿ(M) < ∞ by 1(a). Since π|K_m is a continuous injection of a compact set, x_m := (π|K_m)⁻¹ : π(K_m) → K_m is continuous.
   Countable rectifiability: M ⊆ M₀'' ∪ ⋃_i F_i(ℝⁿ) with Hⁿ(M₀'') = 0 and F_i Lipschitz. So E ⊆ π̃(M) ⊆ π̃(M₀'') ∪ ⋃_i (π̃∘F_i)(ℝⁿ), where Hⁿ(π̃(M₀'')) = 0 by 1(d) and each π̃∘F_i is Lipschitz. Hence every subset of E is countably n-rectifiable.
   Call x ∈ M' good if x is oriented, x ∈ M_{j(k)} with T_xM = T_xN_{j(k)}, and Dπ(x)(T_xM) = T_{π(x)}Σ_k; here k := k(m) for the m with x ∈ K_m. By (c1) and (c2), Hⁿ(M' ∖ good) = 0.

By tangent_locality with (A, B) = (K_m, M), T_xK_m = T_xM for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ K_m; so the Jacobian J^{K_m}_π equals J Hⁿ-a.e. on K_m.    Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M we have ξ_X(x) = ξ̃(x), hence θ(x)ξ_X(x)(ω(π(x))∘Dπ(x)) = θ(x)((∧ₙDπ(x))ξ̃(x))(ω(π(x))). This is 0 on M ∖ M₊ by (c1), and equals θ(x)J(x)ζ̂(x)(ω(π(x))) on M'. By 2(a) and Hⁿ(M₊ ∖ M') = 0,
   Q_π(ω) = ∫_{M'} θ(x)J(x)ζ̂(x)(ω(π(x))) dHⁿ(x).
   Apply (A) to the positive and negative parts of h(x) := θ(x)ζ̂(x)(ω(π(x))). Both have finite integral against J, since |h| ≤ θ·sup_z|ω(z)|_E by (L2). On the fibre over w we have π(x) = w, so
   (B) Q_π(ω) = ∫ V(w)(ω(w)) dHⁿ(w).
  (c6) Tangent planes of the image. Fix k. Apply tangent_locality, with U := ℝ^P, to (A, B) = (E ∩ Σ_k, E) and to (A, B) = (E ∩ Σ_k, Σ_k). So for Hⁿ-a.e. w ∈ E ∩ Σ_k, T_wE exists and equals T_wΣ_k.
   Let Bad_E be the union of three null sets: these countably many exceptional sets; ℝ^P ∖ E₁; and π(M' ∖ good), which is null by 1(a). Since E ⊆ ⋃_k Σ_k, for every w ∈ E ∖ Bad_E the approximate tangent space Π_w := T_wE exists, and Π_w = T_wΣ_k whenever w ∈ Σ_k.
  (c7) Integer multiplicity in the fibres (Simon 3.7–3.8). Let w ∈ E ∖ Bad_E, and fix a unit orientation ζ_w of Π_w. Every x ∈ π⁻¹(w) ∩ M' is good, since w ∉ π(M' ∖ good). If x ∈ K_m and k := k(m), then w = π(x) ∈ Σ_k, so Dπ(x)(T_xM) = T_wΣ_k = Π_w. By (c5) and (L3), ζ̂(x) = ε(x)ζ_w with ε(x) ∈ {1, −1}.    - the Borel function N' : ℝ^P → ℕ, N'(w) := ⌊ν(w) + 1/2⌋, so N'(w) = |m(w)| on E ∖ Bad_E;
   - the Borel map ζ' : ℝ^P → Λ_n, ζ'(w) := ν(w)⁻¹V(w) if ν(w) > 0, and ζ'(w) := 0 otherwise;
   - the carrier C := {w ∈ E : N'(w) ≥ 1}, a Borel set.
   For w ∈ C ∖ Bad_E: m(w) ≠ 0, ζ'(w) = sgn(m(w))ζ_w is a unit orientation of Π_w, and N'(w)ζ'(w) = m(w)ζ_w = V(w). For w ∈ E ∖ (C ∪ Bad_E): m(w) = N'(w) = 0, so V(w) = 0. Off E, V = 0.   (c9) R_Q := (C, N', ζ') is an IMRep in U representing Q_π. We check each field.
   - measurableSet_carrier: C is Borel.
   - carrier_subset: C ⊆ E ⊆ U.
   - rectifiable: C ⊆ E is countably n-rectifiable by (c3).
   - measurable_mult: N' is Borel.
   - mult_pos: N' ≥ 1 on C, by the definition of C.
